title: Construction, Characterization, and Regenerative Application of Self-Assembled Human Mesenchymal Stem Cell Aggregates
protocol: Add 10 mL of prewarmed phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) into a new 15 mL centrifugal tube in a sterile biosafety cabinet.
Remove the freezing tube containing frozen UCMSCs from liquid nitrogen and quickly place it into a 37 °C water bath.
Shake the tube gently to facilitate rapid and thorough cell thawing.
Slightly suspend the cells in the freezing tube.
Transfer all the contents into the centrifuge tube containing 10 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge the sample at 100 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the cells with 10 mL of PBS.
Centrifuge the sample at 100 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the cells with complete alpha-minimum essential medium (α-MEM) containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 584 mg/L glutamine.
Seed the resuspended cells in 10 cm culture dishes at a density of 5 × 10^6 cells per dish.
Add complete α-MEM medium in the dishes to a total volume of 10 mL.
Gently shake the dishes to distribute the cells.
Incubate the dishes at 37 °C with 5% CO2 in a humidified chamber.
After overnight incubation, discard the supernatant medium.
Add 5 mL of PBS to remove nonadherent cells.
Add 10 mL of fresh complete α-MEM medium.
Change the culture media every 2 days.
When the cells reach 80%-90% confluence, discard the supernatant and wash the cells with 5 mL of PBS.
Incubate the cells in 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin-1 mM EDTA at 37 °C for 2 min.
Separate the cells from the dishes without disrupting cell structure when they become round with broken intercellular junctions.
Neutralize the trypsin by adding 4 mL of complete α-MEM medium.
Collect cells repeatedly by pipetting them into a fresh 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 100 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cells with complete α-MEM medium.
Seed the cells in fresh culture dishes or well plates.
Change the culture media every 2 days.
Prepare cell aggregate-inducing media by adding 50 µg/mL vitamin C into α-MEM with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, and 584 mg/L glutamine.
When cells reach 95% confluence, change the media to cell aggregate-inducing media.
Change fresh cell aggregate-inducing media every 2 days.
After 7-10 days of inducing, look for shaped aggregates under the microscope with thick edges separated from the dish bottom.
Discard the culture media and gently wash cells twice with PBS.
Gently push aggregates from the edge to the middle using small sterile forceps.
Seed the cells in 6-well plate at a density of 1 × 10^6 cells per well.
Prepare 2 µM calcein AM and 4 µM EthD-1 working solution using PBS.
Add 0.3% triton to the cells for 5 min, wash with PBS three times.
Wash the cells, aggregates, and dead-inducing cells with PBS twice.
Add 100 μL of PBS and 100 μL of prepared staining solution to each well.
Incubate the sample for 30 min at room temperature (RT).
Wash the sample with PBS twice.
Add 200 μL of 10 µg/mL Hoechst to each well and incubate the sample for 5 min at RT.
Wash the sample with PBS twice.
Observe under a fluorescence microscope.
Seed cells and induce aggregates according to steps 1.2.4 or 1.2.5.
Wash the cells with PBS after the aggregates are formed in step 1.2.4 or 1.2.5.
Fix the cells using glutaraldehyde for at least 4 h.
Wash the samples with PBS.
Dehydrate the samples through a gradient concentration of ethanol from 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, to 100% for each step, lasting 5 minutes.
Treat the samples twice with anhydrous ethanol.
Immerse the aggregates in 3 mL of hexamethyldisilazane for 30 min.
Aspirate all fluid and naturally dry the samples thoroughly.
Stick the dried samples onto the sample table using double-sided carbon tape.
Coat the surface with metal.
Store the sample at room temperature (RT) for several days.
Observe under a scanning electron microscope (SEM).
Replace the sample inside the machine.
Adjust the machine voltage to 5 kV.
Set the focal length to approximately 12 mm.
Adjust the focus bar until a clear picture appears.
Capture images at low magnification.
Adjust the magnification and refocus to obtain higher magnification images.
Fix aggregates obtained in step 1.2.4 or 1.2.5 with 4% paraformaldehyde at 4 °C for at least 24 h.
Wash fixed samples with PBS.
Place the sample into embedding cassettes overnight to rinse with running water.
Dehydrate samples using automatic dehydration machines through gradient ethanol, xylene, and paraffin as per manufacturer's instructions.
Treat samples sequentially with 85% ethanol for 2 h at RT.
Treat samples sequentially with 95% ethanol for 2 h at RT.
Repeat treatment with 95% ethanol for another 2 h at RT.
Treat samples sequentially with 100% ethanol for 2 h at RT.
Treat samples sequentially with 100% ethanol for 1.5 h at RT.
Treat samples sequentially with xylene for 45 min at RT.
Repeat treatment with xylene for another 45 min at RT.
Immerse samples in paraffin for 30 min at RT.
Immerse samples in paraffin for 1.5 h at RT.
Immerse samples in paraffin for 2 h at 60 °C.
Embed samples with paraffin.
Prepare approximately 5 µm thick sections.
Adhere sections to cationic slides.
Dry the slides for 2 h at 45 °C.
Dewax slides sequentially through xylene for 15 min, twice.
Treat slides sequentially with 100%, 90%, 80%, and 70% ethanol (each for 5 min).
Rinse slides slowly with running water for 5 min.
Stain with hematoxylin for 3-5 min.
Rinse stained sections with water to remove excess fluid around the tissue.
Fractionate with ethanol containing 1% hydrochloric acid for 3-5 s and rinse with running water.
Remove excess water around the tissue.
Stain with eosin for 1 min.
Rinse stained sections with running water to remove excess fluid around the tissue.
Dehydrate the sample with 70%, 80%, 90%, and 100% ethanol for 10 seconds each, followed by xylene for 15 minutes twice.
Dry naturally in the fume hood before sealing the sheet.
Add neutral resin drops and seal the slides with coverslips.
Observe under a light microscope.
Stain with Weigert's iron hematoxylin for 5 min, rinse with water, and wipe dry.
Fractionate with ethanol containing 1% hydrochloric acid for 3-5 s and rinse with running water.
Treat with phosphomolybdic acid aqueous solution for 3-5 min.
Directly re-stain with aniline blue solution for 5 min without washing with water.
Treat with 1% glacial acetic acid for 1 min.
Dehydrate the sample with 70%, 80%, 90%, and 100% ethanol for 10 seconds each, followed by xylene for 15 minutes twice.
Dry naturally in the fume hood before sealing the sheet.
Add neutral resin drops and seal the slides with coverslips.
Observe under a light microscope.
Anesthetize the nude mouse by an intraperitoneal injection of 50 mg/kg pentobarbital sodium.
Apply eye ointment to prevent dryness.
Cut out a transverse incision (~3-4 cm) in the skin behind the ears with sterile small scissors after disinfection with iodophor.
Pull the skin forward to expose the cranium.
Lightly draw the edges of the planned defect area with an 11# blade.
Remove a bone fragment to create a circular defect area approximately 4 mm in diameter.
Flush the wound with saline to provide adequate hemostasis.
Dip the aggregates obtained in step 1.2.5 or 1.2.6 with sterile gauze to absorb surface moisture before implantation.
Place the aggregates into the defect area and slightly pressurize to fill the defect.
Replace the skin after pulling to ensure the implant is fixed.
Close the incision with 1/2, 4 × 10 angled stitches and 4-0 sutures.
Place the animals on a rewarming blanket until they are active.
Return the animals into their cage once fully recovered.
